subject: Finexa private deployment - access corridor options and PoC next steps
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@finexa.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finexa private deploy - connectivity constraints / ask

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving toward a private deployment of Redwood in our AWS tenancy and need a firm recommendation for network connectivity patterns. High level constraints:
- Production tier must be SOC2-compliant; network isolation and auditability are required.
- We are multi-region (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 DR) and will have on-prem datacenter presence in Austin for legacy inference hooks.
- Latency target for API calls is <50ms between Finexa backend and Redwood inference endpoints.
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~50 req/s, bursting to ~1.2k req/s for short periods.
- Cost sensitivity for egress and load balancer hours.

Options we've discussed internally: VPC peering (cross-account peering across regions via transit), AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints + NLB), or classic site-to-site VPN to on-prem. We need: recommended primary connectivity choice, fallback plan for regional outages, and a short PoC plan to validate latency and failover.

Can you put together a short advisory + suggested pilot scope? Also looping in our network lead Samir (cc).

—Alex
Alex Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, Finexa

Subject: Re: Finexa private deploy - connectivity constraints / ask

Alex — thanks for laying out the constraints. Short answer up front: we typically recommend a hybrid approach for customers with the profile you described (PrivateLink for secure, auditable production access + site-to-site for on-prem integration and as a low-cost fallback).

I attached a one-page connectivity matrix that maps pros/cons and ballpark monthly cost for each pattern (finexa-connectivity-matrix.pdf). For the PoC I propose:
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): Deploy PrivateLink endpoints in us-west-2, validate latency and auth flows; run load tests to 1.5k req/s.
- Sprint 2 (1 week): Add a site-to-site VPN from Austin datacenter to us-west-2 as a backup path and to test cross-origin on-prem hooks.
- Sprint 3 (1 week): DR test via us-east-1 NLB + replicate PrivateLink endpoints; measure failover times.

Can Karthik and Jordan weigh in on the technical tradeoffs and any caveats? Kimberly, please flag any compliance caveats for PrivateLink vs peering.

Next steps: if that scope looks good I can share a short Statement of Work and schedule a 60-minute technical working session.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@finexa.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Finexa private deploy - connectivity constraints / ask

Alex / team — adding more technical color from the infra side. I'll keep it concise and call out measurable impacts.

Summary (short): Recommend primary = PrivateLink (interface endpoints backed by an NLB per region) + secondary = S2S VPN (IPsec) from Austin for on-prem hooks and emergency egress. Avoid cross-account VPC peering as a primary for this profile because:
- Peering exposes full route table-level connectivity which increases blast radius and makes strict tenant isolation harder.
- Cross-region peering requires a transit/edge device (Transit Gateway) which adds operational overhead and increases egress complexity.

Tradeoffs and numbers:
- PrivateLink (recommended primary)
  - Security: Good — traffic stays on AWS network and you get interface endpoints in your subnets; no route-table propagation to provider VPCs. Easier to meet SOC2 scoping for network isolation and audit logs.
  - Latency: typically adds 1–3 ms compared to cross-account peering when both sides are in same AZ. Cross-AZ or cross-region will add more (10–40ms for region hops). For your <50ms target, design endpoints in the same AZs as the Finexa application pods and colocate NLBs.
  - Cost: Interface endpoints + NLB-hour cost per region; per-GB data processing charges at NLB and interface endpoints. Ballpark: for steady 50 req/s + occasional spikes to 1.2k, estimate $1.5k–$4k/month for endpoints+NLBs (see attached cost sheet).

- VPC Peering / Transit Gateway
  - Security: Peering shares routing; harder to carve strict audit boundaries. Transit Gateway simplifies cross-region but adds TGW-hour + data processing costs.
  - Latency: Lowest intra-region latency when peered within same AZ; cross-region = higher and more variable.
  - Operational: If you anticipate frequent config changes per account, peering is more brittle.

- Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec)
  - Security: Good for on-prem, encrypted over Internet; does not provide the same network-level isolation inside AWS as PrivateLink.
  - Latency: Internet-latency dependent; expect 20–60ms typical Austin -> us-west-2 depending on provider; can be too variable for <50ms SLA for production.
  - Use-case: Good as backup/fallback and for legacy on-prem integrations where re-architecting to cloud-native is not feasible.

Recommendations (practical):
1) Pilot with PrivateLink in us-west-2 only. Create interface endpoints in 2 AZs (A + C), back them with an internal NLB per AZ. Run load tests targeting 1.5k req/s. Capture p95/p99 latencies and bytes/sec.
2) Provision an IPsec S2S VPN from Austin -> us-west-2 as a failover path and to host legacy callbacks during migration.
3) For DR across us-east-1, provision PrivateLink there and use route53 health checks + a small piece of control-plane logic to shift traffic on failover (we can demo).
4) Operational: use VPC flow logs + ALB/NLB access logs + endpoint metrics to feed the Redwood Console for latency/cost dashboards.

Caveats / notes:
- PrivateLink requires per-region endpoints; remember to automate endpoint creation in your infra repo.
- NLB cross-zone load balancing or per-AZ NLBs? Per-AZ NLBs reduce cross-AZ data charges and improve latency but increase management artifacts; I recommend per-AZ internal NLBs for predictable p95 latency.
- We can run a short pilot with synthetic traffic; we'll provide a load script and a small Helm chart to land the test harness in your cluster.

I can put together the exact test plan and the terraform snippets if you want to move forward.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
